title: Spike mitigation pool rebalancing & price-floor experiment (2026)
body:
Purpose:
Short working note that sets up a small, executable experiment to protect run-rate and margin during short, unpredictable token spikes. This is a hybrid of capacity rebalancing and a temporary price-floor to preserve margin while we scale burst pools.

High-level objective:
- Create a 12-week operational playbook that reduces margin erosion during 2x-5x token surges by: (1) rebalancing existing reserved pools across tiers, (2) nudging demand with a soft price-floor on a subset of routes, and (3) phasing 8–12 FTEs of temp headcount for ops and SRE during the worst weeks.

Why now / context:
- Observed multiple short spikes in Q4 2025 where spot capacity and burst reservations were insufficient, leading to fallback to more expensive on-demand infra and temporary margin loss.
- Product teams expect an increasing number of low-latency chat features launching in H1 2026, increasing probability of transient spikes.

Key assumptions (working):
- Baseline sustained demand = 1.0x (monthly avg).
- Spike scenarios modeled at 2.0x, 3.5x, and 5.0x for windows of 6h, 24h, and 72h respectively.
- Current reserved capacity usage = 78% at 95th percentile.
- Price elasticity (worst-case) for small volume-sensitive routes = -0.3 to -0.6. Enterprise/SLAs less elastic (-0.05 to -0.2).
- Temp ops salary blended fully-loaded = $135k FTE/year -> ~$10.6k/month per FTE.

Scenario summary (run-rate economics, illustrative numbers):
- Table columns: scenario | peak multiplier | expected duration | marginal infra delta ($/hr) | estimated lost revenue from soft-floor ($) | ops temp cost per-week ($) | margin delta (bps)
- BAU | 1.0x | - | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0
- Short spike | 2.0x | 6h | 450 | 200 | 0 | -45 bps
- Medium spike | 3.5x | 24h | 2,200 | 1,500 | 7,700 | -180 bps
- Long spike | 5.0x | 72h | 9,600 | 9,000 | 23,000 | -620 bps

Interpretation notes:
- Marginal infra delta estimated from historical on-demand vs reserved price difference and observed kernel-level overheads for runtime scaling.
- Soft-floor revenue losses assume a 15–25% reduction in token volume on the routes we nudge; this is route-specific (see 'route candidates' section).

Headcount/phasing (temporary hires + rebalancing):
- Ops surge pod (6 wks ramp, 6 wks sustain, 4 wks taper): 6 temps (runbooks, manual routing overrides, cost reconciliation).
- SRE burst support (on-call augmentation, automation runbooks): 3 temps for 10 weeks.
- Product liaison (feature gating, communications): 1 contractor (4 weeks).
- Internal rebalancing: move 10% of reserved capacity from low-util legacy models -> burst pool (no hiring, config-only).
- Estimated blended temp cost (peak 10 weeks): 10 FTEs * $10.6k/month * 2.5 months ~= $265k.

Pricing sensitivity experiment (proposed):
- Windowed soft-floor: for selected non-enterprise routes, add a temporary minimal price increase of +8% (soft-floor) that only applies when pool utilization > 85% and forecasted to breach reserved capacity within 6h.
- Measure: delta in token volume (elasticity), revenue, churn signals (errors, latency), and customer support tickets.

Quick lookup table (price points vs expected demand change):
- +0% (control) -> 0% demand change
- +4% -> -2% to -5% demand shift on price-sensitive routes
- +8% -> -5% to -12% demand shift on price-sensitive routes (enterprise largely stable)
- +15% -> -18%+ demand shift (not recommended)

Route candidates (initial list for soft-floor):
- free-tier-chat-std (high elasticity, non-enterprise)
- embeddings-bulk-ingest (moderate elasticity, opportunistic)
- latency-optimized-chat-small (low elasticity, but high cost per token)
- DO NOT include enterprise-tier, compliance-bound private routes

Trigger rules for activation (operator-run & automated):
- Automated triggers: model-pool-utilization > 85% for 15 consecutive minutes AND predicted local load in next 6h > 110% of reserved -> enact soft-floor rollon for selected routes.
- Human gating: if predicted surge > 3.0x or sustained > 24h, require finance + SRE + product signoff to expand soft-floor or reassign reserved capacity beyond 20%.
- Deactivation: utilization < 70% sustained for 30m OR explicit product rollback.

Operational runbook (short):
- Step 0: Pre-announce to Sales/CS that a soft-floor experiment may enter production; provide scripts for refunds and compensations.
- Step 1: Execute reserved->burst rebalancing script (infra team) -> wait 10m -> confirm pool health.
- Step 2: Toggle soft-floor feature flag on selected routes. Monitor latency, error-rate, token-volume.
- Step 3: If volume drop > 15% and revenue drop > 8% in first 30m, rollback and notify exec.
- Step 4: If surge dampened and margin preserved, keep soft-floor and capture telemetry for A/B analysis.

Metrics to capture (minimum):
- token-usage by route (1m granularity), revenue per-route, infra cost per-hour, pool-utilization, latency 95/99, customer support tickets mentioning pricing, number of rollbacks, time-to-recover.

Estimated financial impact (back-of-envelope for a single medium spike):
- Without experiment: infra delta + lost revenue due to throttles/auto-fallback ~= $6.5k for 24h medium spike -> margin hit ~ -180 bps on that day's revenues.
- With experiment (soft-floor + rebalancing + 3 temp ops): expected infra delta reduced by ~40% (less on-demand usage), revenue loss from soft-floor ~ $1.5k, temp costs amortized per-event ~= $1.9k -> net daily margin improvement vs baseline of ~ +60–120 bps for that day.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: customer backlash / CS churn -> Mitigation: limited to non-enterprise routes, pre-announce to CS, automatic rebate backstop for affected heavy users.
- Risk: mis-prediction leading to double-charging or latency spikes -> Mitigation: stage via canary tenants, 10% traffic for first 24h.
- Risk: operational complexity adds toil -> Mitigation: commit automation work to infra team (JIRA FIN-3421).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Validate elasticity numbers against historical A/B test data (assign to Mateo).
- Build simulation run that ties kernel-level scaling (observed infra deltas) to token-level revenue curves (assign to Jamal).
- CS playbook: create canned compensation templates and escalation paths (assign to Priya).
- Exec decision point: approve up to $300k experiment budget and 10 temp FTEs for up to 12 weeks.

Next steps and immediate asks (this week):
- Run a 2-week simulation using last 6 months of spike windows (Jamal + infra) -> due 2026-02-27.
- Draft CS one-pager and Slack notifications (Priya) -> due 2026-03-01.
- Finance sign-off on temp budget (Leah) -> decision required by 2026-03-05.

Notes to self (shorthand):
- keep experiment small, defensible, route-limited; we can scale the playbook horizontally if positive.
- preserve full audit trail of toggles (feature flags) and include token-level infra tagging.

References / links: see linked_artifacts above for simulation repo and JIRA.

-- end working note --
